analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow is caused by an unchecked copy length in DecodeSingleResponse under the OPENSSL_ALL/WOLFSSL_NGINX/WOLFSSL_HAPROXY code path. After GetDateInfo(), it does XMEMCPY(single->status->thisDateParsed.data, single->status->thisDateAsn + localIdx - single->status->thisDateParsed.length, single->status->thisDateParsed.length) (and similarly for nextDateParsed) without validating that parsed.length fits in the destination buffer or that source range is within input bounds. Crafted OCSP date fields can make thisDateParsed.length large, leading to out-of-bounds read from source and/or overwrite of destination. Crash manifests at memcpy in DecodeSingleResponse.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Fuzzer harness fuzzer-wolfssl-ocsp passes attacker-controlled OCSP response bytes directly to OcspResponseDecode(). Input reaches DecodeBasicOcspResponse -> DecodeResponseData -> DecodeSingleResponse. To trigger, the build must include one of OPENSSL_ALL/WOLFSSL_NGINX/WOLFSSL_HAPROXY (where thisDateParsed/nextDateParsed memcpy exists). A malformed SingleResponse date encoding that yields an excessive length via GetDateInfo causes memcpy with attacker-controlled length, producing the observed heap-buffer-overflow.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/wolfcrypt/src/asn.c
+++ b/wolfcrypt/src/asn.c
@@ -33758,6 +33758,10 @@
                     (byte*)&single->status->thisDateParsed.type,
                     &single->status->thisDateParsed.length, size) < 0)
         return ASN_PARSE_E;
+    if ((word32)single->status->thisDateParsed.length > localIdx ||
+            single->status->thisDateParsed.length >
+            (word32)sizeof(single->status->thisDateParsed.data))
+        return BUFFER_E;
     XMEMCPY(single->status->thisDateParsed.data,
             single->status->thisDateAsn + localIdx - single->status->thisDateParsed.length,
             single->status->thisDateParsed.length);
@@ -33790,6 +33794,10 @@
                         (byte*)&single->status->nextDateParsed.type,
                         &single->status->nextDateParsed.length, size) < 0)
             return ASN_PARSE_E;
+        if ((word32)single->status->nextDateParsed.length > localIdx ||
+                single->status->nextDateParsed.length >
+                (word32)sizeof(single->status->nextDateParsed.data))
+            return BUFFER_E;
         XMEMCPY(single->status->nextDateParsed.data,
                 single->status->nextDateAsn + localIdx - single->status->nextDateParsed.length,
                 single->status->nextDateParsed.length);
